subject: Hormuz physical-flow state sharpens: weekend traffic ~90% below pre-conflict baseline
body_md: Thesis: the strongest current Hormuz state variable is now direct physical vessel throughput, not official rhetoric. Reuters reported fewer than 20 commodity-vessel transits over the weekend, with traffic roughly 90% below pre-conflict baselines; Iran separately blacklisted 45 tankers and warned that STS counterparties can inherit penalties. This strengthens the existing `physical throughput + permission regime` model, but does not resolve exact oil-volume estimates because some AIS can be disabled. Conviction: +0.84. Supporting evidence: Reuters Aug. 24 vessel-flow report and Reuters Aug. 24 blacklist report. Contradiction/uncertainty: transponder-off traffic can cause undercounting; official U.S. throughput claims remain materially higher than tracker estimates. What would falsify this: sustained recovery in independently observed vessel traffic plus downstream refinery/product delivery data converging with official throughput estimates. Product implication: update Orbital Insight to display baseline-vs-current transit ratio and source-methodology conflict as first-class fields, rather than one headline throughput number.
